learning_outcomes.text: Identifies fundamental concepts specific to the electrical field with applicability in mechanical engineering.
Explains the fundamental elements and stages of a characteristic analysis of electrical circuits and equipment with applicability in mechanical engineering.
Identifies theories for analyzing electrical circuits and compares specific results of electrical phenomena.
Identifies methods for testing electrical circuits and equipment for measuring and testing specific parameters.
Uses instruments for performing analysis and testing work on electrical circuits and equipment specific to the electrical field.
Plans the measurement of electrical quantities and understands the use of different instrumental methods.
Operates laboratory equipment used for measuring various electrical quantities.
Critically evaluates processes, equipment, and procedures specific to the electrical field using specific evaluation instruments and methods.

Respects ethical principles, norms, and values in the correct and timely execution of professional tasks, by adopting a rigorous, efficient, and responsible work strategy in decision-making for problem-solving.
Integrates into the work group and applies effective relationship and work techniques in multidisciplinary teams, across various hierarchical levels.
Continuously informs and documents oneself in one's own field of activity by adequately using efficient learning methods and techniques.
Develops professional projects in the field of engineering.

syllabus_topics: DC electrical circuits: Electrical energy sources. Electric current. DC electrical circuit. Ohm's Law. Electrical resistance.
DC electrical circuits: Electrical energy and power. Joule-Lenz Law. Calculation of complex linear DC circuits. Kirchhoff's Theorems.
Magnetic circuits: definitions, structure, classification. Ferromagnetic materials.
Magnetic circuits: Magnetic field energy: energy losses in metallic bodies introduced into variable magnetic fields. Forces in the magnetic field.
AC electrical circuits: Sinusoidal signals, characteristic values. Symbolic representation of sinusoidal signals.
AC electrical circuits: Circuit elements in steady-state sinusoidal regime.
AC electrical circuits: Series and parallel RLC circuits, electrical resonance. Analysis of branched linear electrical circuits in steady-state sinusoidal regime.
AC electrical circuits: Powers in AC circuits in sinusoidal regime.
Three-phase electrical circuits: definitions, classification. Three-phase circuit connections. Powers in three-phase circuits. Power factor: economic importance, improvement methods.
Electrical transformers: Generalities: classification, construction, nominal quantities, conventional symbols.

Single-phase transformer: operation, transformation ratio. No-load operation: equations, equivalent circuit. Load operation: equations. Referenced single-phase transformer: equations, equivalent circuit. Single-phase transformer power and losses. Tests: no-load and short-circuit tests. External characteristic. Transformer efficiency: separate losses method.

General problems of AC machines: Classification of electrical machines. Common constructive elements. Magnetic field created by AC machine windings: magnetic field created by a single-phase (pulsating) winding, three-phase rotating magnetic field, two-phase rotating magnetic field.

Asynchronous electrical machines: Three-phase asynchronous machine: construction, operating regimes, nominal quantities, conventional symbols. Equivalent circuit of the asynchronous motor. Power losses and efficiency of the asynchronous motor: energy diagram. Electromagnetic torque of the three-phase asynchronous motor. Natural mechanical characteristic M = f(s). Artificial mechanical characteristics. Stability of the three-phase asynchronous motor. Starting of the three-phase asynchronous motor.

DC electrical machines: General notions: classification, constructive elements, nominal quantities, conventional symbols. Inductor field of the DC machine. Generator operation: role of the commutator-brush system; calculation of EMF. Load operation: armature reaction; commutation of DC machines. Operating characteristics of DC generators. Motor operation: role of the commutator-brush system, electromagnetic torque, voltage equation. Starting of DC motors. Series excited DC motor. Shunt/separately excited DC motor.
1. a. Occupational safety and health and fire prevention norms in the laboratory b. Elements of DC electrical circuits
2. Experimental study of DC circuits
3. Experimental study of the series RLC circuit.
4. Power factor improvement.
5. Three-phase electrical circuits.
6. Single-phase transformer.
7. Three-phase asynchronous motor with short-circuited rotor.
teaching_methods: Participatory lectures and debates based on PowerPoint presentations
Discovery learning models facilitated by direct and indirect exploration of reality (experiment, demonstration, modeling)
Action-based methods, such as exercises, practical activities, and problem-solving.
assessment_rules: Students must participate in practical laboratory work and submit laboratory assignments on time. A minimum grade of 5 must be obtained in the final exam.
